text: #359's runtime contracts and conformance, for @gitdek's ratification, in place of D-0224 after #359's review. A module that holds a selected function imports nagini_contracts to state its contract, so the application must ship Invariant's runtime stand-in, byte for byte: the gate checks that the application root's nagini_contracts package holds exactly the stand-in's __init__.py and contracts.py, and refuses anything else, an installed distribution included, once the session has staged the application, before any test, conformance, backing test or Nagini runs. Any other nagini_contracts could rebind a name the proof relies on, as a min shadowing the builtin does, or give the contract calls that run inside the proved body effects Nagini assumes away, and the one distribution that provides it, Nagini itself, returns None from Result(). The stand-in's Result() returns an inert value, since Python evaluates a contract call's argument before the call, so a contract such as Ensures(Result() >= count) runs without effect. A selected function may read only the Nagini names the stand-in exports, since only those are bound where the application runs, so a selection that reads any other, as ToSeq, is refused; Assume is refused too, since it has Nagini take a fact nothing proves. A check that selects an in-place proof must also select conformance, and its proof qualifies only when that conformance passed, since the collector's binding of what conformance observes to the function's staged declaration is how the gate shows the function Nagini proved is the one the application runs.
